item.content:encoded: Shaggy already covered most of the criticisms I have of this, but I'll take a moment to add that the tone of the memos is comically villainous, to the point of absurdity. I can guarantee that there is not a person alive who would begin an official report of any kind with "My my my my my." item.content:encoded:
Accept for the part of Carter idea go wrong, it's very similar to one more MC&D delicacy, which is also a rear egg on the plate.

Spelling errors aside, the objects may be similar, but the story is completely different. I wrote the Fossil Eggs for the History Contest, where it was in the context of the bitter rivalry between E.D. Cope and O.C. Marsh having what could have been their greatest discovery stolen by agents of Marshall, Carter and Dark.

This isn't ripping it off at all. The author gave more thought and care to the correspondence between those involved in MC&D business than I did in Imperfectly Preserved Fossil Eggs, and is a self-contained story, where as what I wrote requires the context of an entirely different work in order to be fully understood. (P.S.: whoever runs the MC&D template, please make in-text links stand out more. You can barely see them.) This stands alone in the War on All Fronts canon, and as a tale on its own.

To be blunt: I don't think you know what you're talking about.

But lately it somehow go soft. It began to tolerate more and more. Not in good sense.

item.content:encoded:
"Duplication" implies intentional copying…

I didn't mean intentional. Although I may use a wrong word. If so i want to apologize for it.
I even consider maybe authors didn't even know the other works exist, so much content is on site now.

But in my way of thinking if you making some form of art or any creation, about some ideas which allready been "explored" by someone before you, you have to make some distinctive qualities in performance or explore the idea in some new unexplored way or make a difference in any other way. Otherwise it would be "industrial mass production" or even "Chinese industrial mass production". Machines are good at it. And people in mass love good mass-produced product. Phones. Cars. Shoes.
Steady suply, steady quality.

For exemple:
The Black Square by Kazimir Malevich is world-famous pice of art. Black Circle, Red Square and a bunch of his own late works not known by the public at large not because they kept in secret.

Of course the main yardstick of art is the audience reception. And it's been the foundation guiding star, which lead this community to today prosperity.
But lately it somehow go soft. It began to tolerate more and more. Not in good sense.
Sometimes works wich would be downvoted in to oblivion a few years ago. (I want to make a note, what i dont imply this very one work).
Someone posted a scp which is literally "deathnote ink bottle" more then a year ago. With demonic scriming and other staff, not even written in good clinic tone. And it's still somethere here.

I mean no offense to you or the autors of any of mentioned work.
Discussion page is here so any one can discus any pice of work, and give the authors the feedback about what is good and what is bad from his point of view. Maybe for improvment of current work, maybe for later use and consideration.
How to use gotten feedback is totaly the authors choise. Even to read or not to read the feedback is each author own choise.
If some of them will see my point and will consider it for later works my feedback will have a reasult. If not, it would be a sign to me that world has changed.

item.content:encoded:
And it does not have any outstanding features of it's own. So it's basically a not very good copy.

Wouldn't it be a bad thing if it was a "good copy"? It's distinct enough for people to enjoy it, and if they like both, they can upvote both. They shouldn't feel pressured to like only one or the other.

P.S. For some reason it's not the first duplication work which came recently. Ancient war elephant made by a team of very famous authors has the same problem.

"Duplication" implies intentional copying, which I believe is not the case of the article you're referring to here. Furthermore, there's no rule on the site that states similar works cannot exist. We have tons of dog and cat and humanoid articles, but that doesn't mean that nothing similar can ever be written ever again.

And strangely to me has a very high rate.

Is it surprising that if lots of people like something, there are a lot of upvotes?

I just hope this is not new thread of community.

If you feel an inherent loyalty to the first of a kind of written work and dislike all similar subsequent writings, that's your prerogative. However, the site's general rule when it comes to writing is "if the audience likes it, it stays".

item.content:encoded:
Because I apparently set myself up as a stawman with that line, I feel as though I should rephrase somewhat. That line by itself, while immersion-breaking enough to downvote at the point in which it appears, is not enough to write off the entire article, which could very well have been written well enough for me to change my mind.

What cemented my vote, to reiterate, is the barebones predictable plot. That there was some attempt at lampshading the obvious development (with the Sarkites) didn't do enough to make it an entertaining read. It's another article in the canon simply plugging group archetypes into articles, reinforcing the supposedly shaken status quo.

As an aside, unless the character is a former SH operative, I don't know why they'd refer to the GOC as 'bookburners', which is where that nickname originates from.

That's fair as well. My response to that would be that Ruprecht's avoided capture for so long because he's rich, not because he's smart (Trump, basically). The financial and anomalous resources at MC&D's disposal make them a force to be reckoned with, and are more than sufficient to get their board members out of any jams they may end up in.

Whenever MC&D pops up in Dread & Circuses (which this technically isn't but I'm still counting it in that continuity) Percival/Iris are the brains of the operation, Amos Marshall is the shrewd businessman, and Carter is a Rich Idiot With No Day Job.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My downvote fell right at the "UIUseless", which elicited a heavy eyeroll.

Yeah, I think that's where most of the other downvotes came from as well. Kalinin even mentioned it in the base article. The reason I did that is that I do think UIU were kind of useless in this scenario. They're unable to prevent the GOC from luring the Kaiju to 3ports, then demand they leave without cleaning up their mess, and then bring in MC&D of all groups to haul off the corpse and don't charge them anywhere near enough for the privilege. I felt it would be well within Ruprecht's character to mock them for this.

I understand your reasons for downvoting and respect it, but I'm going to leave the line in.

I think you're right about this canon not reaching it's full potential. It's a wide-reaching event, sure, but so far it hasn't been that iconoclastic. It's just another anomaly for the GoIs to squabble over, albeit a really big one. Most of the authors for the canon haven't posted yet, so hopefully future works might go further into that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is definitely the best submission for this series so far, being more focused and offering some genuine character interaction. My downvote fell right at the "UIUseless", which elicited a heavy eyeroll.

Using the memey out-of-universe name which jokingly refers to a stereotype for a that group doesn't do much to build confidence that there's going to be anything much in the way of creative use of said groups, so once the Sarkites showed up, it was pretty easy to guess where it was going to go, so the story ended up being rather predictable.

As an aside, this was pitched as some large event that would quote "rock the anomalous world", which really is certainly intriguing, but as I warned when I first heard of the concept, it's not giving that impression in the slightest. Everyone is doing exactly what one would expect each group to do. Each GoI is operating very strictly n the confines of their respective bit parts. There hasn't been any novel use or changes to speak of, and I'm feeling let down on the promise of such a massive paradigm-shifting event.

Hoping subsequent entries begin to surprise me.
